correctness.rationale: For one-sign maximality H=A(F_p2)[p+1] is a subgroup with |H| dividing both the actual group order and the Hasse upper endpoint (p+1)^(2g). If |H| exceeded interval width W_g(p)=(p+1)^(2g)-(p-1)^(2g), the two multiples would coincide; nonmaximal cases thus have |H|<=W. Divide by lower bound (p-1)^(2g), clip at 1, and power the conditional bound for k independent samples. The minimality branch is symmetric using p-1. Expansion gives W_g(p)=4g p^(2g-1)+2sum_{r=1}^{g-1} C(2g,2r+1)p^(2g-2r-1) for g>=2, strictly larger than the proof's substituted 4g p^(2g-1). The original arXiv:2610.01924v1 Theorem 4.1 p20 was read and its displayed inequality directly shows the incorrect smaller constant. No claim smaller bound intrinsically impossible by a different structural theorem.
residual_risks: Corrected width bound is not claimed sharp; additional geometric restrictions could validate a smaller false-positive constant by a different argument.
